extracted.intended_audience: laboratory technicians, veterinary surgeons, and researchers performing experimental animal inoculations
extracted.subtask_description: Detailed procedural and aseptic guidelines for preparing, handling, and inoculating laboratory animals by multiple routes (cutaneous, subcutaneous, intramuscular, intraperitoneal, intracranial, intraocular, intrapulmonary, intravenous), plus apparatus, animal care, and specimen preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary inspection and examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The preliminary examination should comprise observation of the animal at rest and in motion; the appearance of the fur, feathers or scales, inspection of the eyes, and of external orifices of the body; tactile examination of the body and limbs, and palpation of the groins and abdomen; and in many cases the microscopical examination of fresh and stained blood-films.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform careful visual and tactile checks and microscopy where indicated to detect naturally acquired infections before experiments; inspection informs suitability for use and need for segregation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Segregation and treatment of parasitic infections
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is decided to try and save animals suffering from infection by these parasites, they must be segregated, the scabs carefully cleaned from the infected areas and the denuded surfaces washed with 5 per cent. solution of Potassium persulphate, or with a preparation containing equal parts of soft paraffin and vaseline with a few drops of lysol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeat treatment daily until acarus destroyed; disinfect cages and examine/treat neighbouring animals; specific sites of infection described (eg. ears, groins) and signs (scales, crusts, pain when lifted by ears).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tuberculosis testing on arrival
rubrics_metrics.description: Test animals as soon as they reach the laboratory by injecting Koch's Old Tuberculin: 0.5 c.c. for guinea pigs (causing death in the tuberculous cavy within 48 hours); 1 c.c. for monkeys.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Old Tuberculin dosing on arrival to identify tuberculous animals before inclusion in experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighing technique and appropriate scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Larger animals weighed on a decimal scale with metal cage; mice and rats weighed on a modification of the letter balance to 250 grammes with a conical wire cage carefully counterpoised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use suitable cages attached to scales (avoid ordinary pan), counterpoise appropriately; provide species-appropriate weighing apparatus (figures referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Temperature measurement procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: To take rectal temperature: animal held carefully; introduce bulb of clinical thermometer greased with vaseline just within sphincter ani, then push until entire bulb and part of stem have passed into rectum; allow 3–5 minutes before reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify thermometers periodically against a standard Kew certified Thermometer kept in the laboratory; timing varies with thermometer sensibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cage and accommodation standards
rubrics_metrics.description: During the period between inoculation and death or recovery, experimental animals must be kept in suitable receptacles which can easily be kept clean and readily disinfected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Species-specific recommendations: mice in glass jars with wire gauze covers and sand-blasted labels; rats in larger jars; rabbits and guinea-pigs in metal woven-wire cages with movable metal tray for excreta and raised on legs; trays cleaned daily and soiled sawdust cremated; cages sterilised by autoclaving or formalin spray.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bedding and feeding requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide sawdust or plentiful straw for bedding; mice/rats: bran and oats with occasional bread-and-milk; rabbits/guinea-pigs: fresh vegetables (cabbage, carrot, turnip tops) morning and broken animal biscuits evening; water in earthenware dish occasionally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure bedding absorbs moisture; provide bedding that allows animals to self-clean (eg. straw for mice) and maintain food hygiene to reduce infection risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asepsis of inoculation as a surgical operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Animal inoculation is purely a surgical operation; necessary instruments must be sterile and strict attention must be paid to asepsis; hands of the operator should be carefully disinfected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt same sterile discipline as human surgery; sterilise instruments before use and disinfect after use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apparatus list and syringe sterilisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use water steriliser(s); injection syringes (1 c.c. hypodermic with asbestos washers preferred) must be easily disassembled; to sterilise syringe, fill with water, loosen packing and screw joints, place in steriliser and boil for at least five minutes; disinfect after use similarly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep spare parts/needles; needles should be stored in absolute alcohol to avoid rusting; maintain supply of various syringe sizes (2, 5, 10, 20 c.c.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sterilisation and storage of surgical instruments and consumables
rubrics_metrics.description: Surgical instruments sterilised by boiling and disinfected after use by the same means; wipe perfectly dry immediately after disinfection. Sterile cotton-wool is packed loosely in a copper cylinder and sterilised in the hot-air oven. Gauze sterilised similarly. Sterilised silk and catgut boiled for about ten minutes in the water steriliser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dry instruments promptly to prevent damage; store needles in alcohol; maintain sterile glass capsules and pipettes of specified sizes for handling inoculum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anaesthetic recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: General anaesthetic: A.C.E. mixture freshly prepared by volume—alcohol 1 part, chloroform 2 parts, ether 6 parts—administered on a 'cone' of towel/cotton-wool; Local anaesthetics: cocaine hydrochloride 2% in adrenalin 1 per mille; beta-eucaine 2% in adrenalin 1 per mille; ethyl chloride jet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select anaesthesia according to procedure and species; prepare A.C.E. freshly; local options listed for ocular/local procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skin preparation and depilation
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply liquid soap (recipe provided) to fur, lather and shave thoroughly or use depilatory powder (barium sulphide 1 part, rice starch 3 parts) applied, wetted to paste, acted 3 minutes and scraped off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After depilation, wash denuded area with 2% lysol solution, then wash off lysol with ether and allow evaporation before incision or inoculation; depilatory preferred day before operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of inoculum material
rubrics_metrics.description: Material inoculated may be (1) cultures of bacteria (fluid or solid), (2) metabolic products of bacterial activity (toxins in solution), or (3) pathological products (fluid secretions/excretions, solid tissues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each class has specific preparation and handling procedures detailed in subsequent entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of inoculum from fluid cultures
rubrics_metrics.description: Flame culture tube plug and mouth, pour cultivation into sterile capsule, cool sterilised syringe and draw required amount into barrel; or use sterile graduated pipette; for large volumes transfer to sterile separatory funnel graduated if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain aseptic technique throughout (flaming, sterile containers); when using separatory funnel, attach sterilised tubing with needle and screw clamp; for some routes a 'fall' suffices, for subcutaneous use pressure apparatus (wash-bottle + hand bellows with air filter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of inoculum from solid media and viscous/pathological products
rubrics_metrics.description: Emulsify growth from sloped agar with sterile bouillon using sterile platinum loop to convert to fluid inoculum; viscous secretions may be diluted with sterile bouillon/saline and emulsified; solid tissues may be minced and ground in sterilised agate mortar with bouillon to make an emulsion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solid sections intended for implantation en masse: remove 1–2 mm cube and introduce into wound with sterile instruments; close wound with Michel's steel clips and sealed dressing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preventing embolism and air injection for intravenous inoculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation of the inoculum: care must be taken as injection of even small fragments may cause fatal embolism. To obviate this risk the fluid should, if possible, be filtered through sterile filter paper before filling into the syringe. Air bubbles, when injected into a vein, frequently cause immediate death; to prevent this hold the syringe vertical with needle uppermost, impale sterile filter paper on the needle and press piston upward until all air is expelled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filter fluids destined for IV injection to remove fragments; remove all air from syringe before venous puncture using described technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods of securing animals during inoculation
rubrics_metrics.description: For most inoculations an assistant holds the animal; for single-handed work use Voge's holder for guinea-pigs (hollow copper cylinder with ventilating holes and removable cap) or metal holders for mice with tail spring clip; holders should be entirely metal and wire cages detachable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two sizes of Voge's holder recommended (dimensions given); when anaesthetised secure animals to an operating table such as Tatin's or author's operating table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating table specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an 'aseptic' table of steel tubing, nickel-plated or enamelled; frame sufficiently large for rabbits, dogs and monkeys; supported on telescopic uprights to adjust height; table-top frame inclinable to 45° and rotatable about its long axis; top composed of copper wire gauze loosely suspended to permit hot-water bottle or electrotherm under animal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design permits reversal of animal by rotating frame and reversing gauze; use appropriate tables for species size and required access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cutaneous inoculation technique
rubrics_metrics.description: No anaesthetic. Steps: hold animal; apply liquid soap and shave or depilate; wash denuded skin with 2% lysol; wash off lysol with ether and allow to evaporate; make numerous short parallel superficial incisions with sterile scalpel; when oozing ceased, rub inoculum into scarifications with flat scalpel or sterile spatula; cover with pad of sterile gauze secured by adhesive plaster or sealed with collodion; release animal and affix label with distinctive name/number, weight, source and dose of inoculum, and date of inoculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure thorough skin prep and sterile covering; label cage with required data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcutaneous inoculation (fluid and solid) technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Fluid (no anaesthetic): shave and disinfect as for cutaneous; pinch fold of skin, insert needle so ~2 cm lies in subcutaneous tissue, inject slowly, withdraw needle and close puncture with cotton wool; label. Solid (none or ethyl chloride): make small incision, use probe to form funnel-shaped pocket, deposit small piece of inoculum deep in pocket, close wound with Michel's clips and sealed dressing, label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For solid inoculation an improvised glass tube syringe may be used to deposit tissue; follow asepsis and post-op dressing protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intramuscular inoculation (fluid and solid) technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Fluid (no anaesthetic): steady skin over selected muscle and thrust needle into muscle injecting slowly. Solid (anaesthetic A.C.E.): secure and anaesthetise animal, shave and disinfect, surround field with gauze in 2% lysol, incise skin/aponeurosis/muscle, deposit inoculum deep, close muscle with buried sutures and skin with continuous/interrupted sutures or Michel's clips, apply sealed dressing, release animal and label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe aseptic wound closure techniques appropriate to muscle and skin layers; use anaesthesia for deeper implants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intraperitoneal inoculation techniques (fluid and solid)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fluid (no anaesthetic): shave broad transverse area flank to flank, pinch up triangular fold ensuring no intestine included, transfix near base so needle lies free in peritoneal cavity and inject. Alternate: anaesthetise small skin area with ethyl chloride, heat platinum searing wire to burn hole through skin and abdominal muscle down to but not through visceral peritoneum, push blunt-ended needle through into peritoneal cavity and inject. Solid (anaesthetic A.C.E.): laparotomy with midline incision, divide aponeuroses and peritoneum, introduce inoculum, close peritoneum with Lembert's sutures, close skin and aponeurosis with interrupted sutures or Michel's clips and sealed dressing; label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using burned aperture, can sample peritoneal fluid intermittently; ensure no intestinal injury and proper closure for solid implantation; label after procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and use of collodion and celloidin sacs for peritoneal implantation
rubrics_metrics.description: Collodion sacs: form by dipping test-tube into collodion several times, peel off, attach to glass tubing, incubate 24h to adhere, sterilise in hot-air oven, fill with cultivation and tie off before insertion. Celloidin sacs: make from gelatine capsules coated with celloidin, attach quill glass tubing, fill, seal, test impermeability by incubation in broth before insertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test sacs' impermeability by incubating in broth overnight; use sterile technique when filling and sealing; detailed stepwise manufacture provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intracranial inoculation and trephine use
rubrics_metrics.description: Use small nasal trephine (Curtis) with tooth cutting circle 7 mm and adjustable collar guard to prevent accidental laceration of dura or brain; smaller sizes (6 and 4 mm) for guinea pigs; for very small animals use dental drill. Subdural: anaesthetise, reflect crescentic scalp flap, remove circular piece of bone (trephine centre at median line intersecting line joining posterior canthi), perforate dura with needle and deposit material immediately below membrane avoiding sinuses, close and dress. Intracerebral: same but push needle into cerebral hemisphere substance before ejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use surgical engine (Guy's dental engine) for speed and safety; avoid dural/vascular injury; close scalp with Michel's clips and sealed dressing; label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intraocular inoculation techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Fluid (anaesthetic cocaine): instil sterile cocaine drops, repeat after 2 minutes, five minutes later hold animal, sterilise two needles to same syringe, pierce cornea with one needle allowing aqueous to escape, attach syringe and inject into anterior chamber, irrigate conjunctival sac with sterile saline, label. Solid (anaesthetic A.C.E.): anaesthetise and secure, irrigate conjunctival sac, incise upper cornea with triangular keratome, separate wound lips with silver spatula, introduce solid inoculum with iris forceps onto anterior surface of iris, irrigate, release animal, label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use topical cocaine for fluid anterior chamber injections; irrigate after injection; follow asepsis rigorously to avoid ocular infection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intrapulmonary inoculation technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Fluid inoculum (no anaesthetic): have animal firmly held, draw foreleg up and hold with ear, shave in axillary line and disinfect, thrust needle through fifth or sixth intercostal space into lung tissue and inject contents of syringe slowly, label.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure accurate anatomical landmarking (5th/6th intercostal space) and secure restraint to avoid misplacement; practise aseptic skin preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intravenous inoculation site selection and preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Rabbit: posterior auricular vein preferred; guinea-pig: jugular vein (general anaesthetic required); monkey/dog: internal saphenous vein (distend by compressing vein above site). Prepare inoculum by filtering to avoid fragments that could cause embolism, remove air bubbles before injection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose vein appropriate to species; render vein prominent if needed; filter and de-air syringe before venous puncture; follow species-specific anaesthesia guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-procedure labelling requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Affix a label upon which is written: (a) Distinctive name or number of the animal, (b) Its weight, (c) Particulars as to source and dose of inoculum, (d) Date of inoculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach label to cage after release of animal; maintain records for traceability of inoculation events.
